text: The user has been experiencing slow internet speeds, especially when working from home, and is considering calling their internet provider to negotiate a better deal.
The user recently got a new router on January 15th, which has improved their Wi-Fi signal strength significantly, but the user still needs to figure out how to set up the guest network feature.

The assistant recommended checking internet speed with online tools such as Speedtest.net, reviewing the current internet plan, restarting the router, and checking the provider's website or social media for reported outages in the area.

The assistant advised moving devices that use the same frequency band, such as cordless phones and microwaves, away from the router, and placing the router in a central, elevated location clear of obstacles to maximise signal strength.

The assistant advised that before calling the provider the user should know their plan details including speed tier and pricing, explain the slow speeds clearly, ask about current promotions, and ask for a supervisor or retention specialist if not satisfied.
The assistant said guest network instructions can usually be found in the router's user manual or in online documentation for the router.

The user restarted the router, but slow speeds persisted, and the user checked for outages and found no reported issues in their area, so they planned to check their plan details and optimise router placement as suggested.
The user asked whether it is worth switching to a different internet service provider if they are not satisfied with their current one.

The assistant suggested comparing other ISPs with tools such as BroadbandNow or Allconnect, checking bundles, reading reviews and promotions, and considering data caps, throttling, fees and customer service. It also advised checking installation fees and early termination fees in the contract, cancelling the current service, and returning any rented equipment to avoid extra charges.

The user said they will consider switching if not satisfied and are unsure whether their current plan suits their needs. The user paid their internet bill on January 25th, which reminded them to call the provider to negotiate a better deal.

The assistant advised the user, when calling the provider, to explain how slow speeds affect their productivity, know their speed tier, data allowance and pricing, ask about upgrades such as fibre-optic, and take notes of the call.
The user uses their smart speaker to play music, set reminders and make hands-free calls, and wants to learn what else it can do and how to get the most out of it.

The assistant listed smart speaker features including controlling lights, thermostats, security cameras and door locks, recipes and unit conversions, news and podcasts, calendar management, translation, games, and shopping and order tracking. It also noted fitness tracking, meditation, and custom routines such as a Goodnight routine that locks doors, turns off lights and adjusts the thermostat.

The user said their smart speaker batteries are running low and they need to reorder them. The user wants to create custom routines that turn off lights when leaving the house and lock the doors at night.

The assistant gave steps to create a routine in the companion app: open the Routines or Automation section, create a new routine, choose a trigger such as a voice command, location, time of day or an event, add and configure actions, then save the routine and test it.
The user ordered cable organizers online on January 28th to tidy up messy cords and cables, but they had not arrived yet, and the user finds it frustrating to find the right charger every day.

The assistant suggested exploring the smart speaker's companion app, checking for software updates, browsing the Skills or Actions section, and trying different voice commands to discover new features.
The user is considering setting up a small art studio in their spare bedroom and asked for tips on organising a small space for painting and storing supplies.
The assistant advised purging and decluttering the room before setting up, and assessing the types of art and supplies the user will need so they can choose the right layout and storage solutions.

The assistant recommended a U-shaped or L-shaped workstation to maximise counter space, placing the main work surface in a well-lit spot away from direct sunlight, and leaving enough room to move around comfortably.

For storage, the assistant suggested shelving units, bookcases or storage cubes, stackable bins and baskets, and pegboards, hooks or bulletin boards on the walls. It advised grouping supplies by category and labelling each container or shelf.

The assistant suggested a worktable with built-in drawers, shelves or cabinets, a good task light or LED overhead lighting, an ergonomic chair, and a standing desk or riser if needed, and recommended personalising the space with plants or inspiring artwork.
The user's sister's birthday is next month, in September 2023, and the user is working on gift ideas for her, including possibly a painting.

The assistant suggested painting gift ideas including a personalised portrait, a special place such as a childhood home, a favourite animal, a floral or botanical piece, or an abstract piece. It also suggested a painting of a shared memory or inside joke, an inspirational quote, or a piece in the sister's favourite colours.

The user is working on a sunset scene painting that they think their sister will love. The user has completed four projects since starting painting classes and feels pretty confident about their skills.

The assistant recommended varnishes made for artworks, such as dammar varnish, Liquitex Soluvar or Golden MSA Varnish, preferably with UV protection, and noted that acrylic and oil paintings need different varnishes.

The assistant advised that a painting must be completely dry and cured before varnishing, which can take a few days to several weeks. It suggested dusting the surface and lightly sanding if needed, then applying varnish in thin, even layers in a well-ventilated area away from direct sunlight, working from the top down and avoiding the edges.
The assistant suggested framing the painting with acid-free materials and UV-filtering glass, and handling it carefully away from extreme temperatures, humidity and direct sunlight.
The user asked how to sign and date a painting without detracting from the overall piece.

The assistant advised signing in a discreet corner, usually the lower right or left, using a harmonious and legible font, keeping a consistent signature style, and dating the year the painting was completed rather than the year it was started.

The user has completed four projects since starting painting classes and follows several artists on Instagram who inspire them. The user asked how to reach out to them or engage with their content in a meaningful way.

The assistant advised liking and thoughtfully commenting on artists' posts, not messaging them excessively, avoiding requests for free critiques, showing genuine interest in their work, and building a relationship over time.

The user is thinking of reaching out to @artbylisa, who posted a tutorial on creating a galaxy effect using acrylics. The user tried the technique on Tuesday evening, 15 August 2023 (last Tuesday evening), with imperfect results, and plans to experiment more with it.

The assistant advised the user to be honest and humble about the imperfect result, describe the steps taken and challenges faced, ask specific questions, attach a photo of the attempt, and be patient because @artbylisa may not reply quickly.
The user has just finished their fifth project since starting painting classes, feels pretty accomplished, and is looking for ideas or themes for their next painting project.

The assistant suggested painting themes including nature escapes such as mountains, beaches and wildlife, cityscapes and nightscapes, abstract expressions, fantasy and whimsy, figurative art, still life, pop culture and nostalgia, and personal symbolism.
The user said they like the idea of exploring abstract expressions and asked for tips on creating a good abstract piece.

The assistant's abstract painting tips included letting go of control, experimenting with acrylics, oils, watercolours, palette knives and sponges, starting with a loose gesture, and building layers through glazing and scumbling.

The assistant also advised adding texture with impasto or collage, emphasising movement and energy, and stepping back regularly to evaluate balance. It named Jackson Pollock, Willem de Kooning, Mark Rothko, Franz Kline, Joan Mitchell and Helen Frankenthaler as abstract expressionists to draw inspiration from.
The user said they like the idea of using a limited palette and asked for colour combinations that would work well for an abstract piece.

The assistant suggested limited palettes including monochromatic blues, greens or earth tones, analogous blue-green-yellow or red-orange-yellow, complementary pairs such as blue and orange, red and green, or yellow and purple, and neutral palettes of black, white and grey.
The assistant suggested bold and bright palettes built from primary colours with black or white, bright pastels such as hot pink, electric blue and lime green, or neon colours on a dark background.
The user said they like a bold and bright palette, have always been drawn to vibrant colours, and asked for tips on balancing bold colours so they don't overwhelm the piece.

The assistant advised starting with a dominant bold colour, using a neutral background, balancing warm and cool colours, varying saturation, adding a unifying element, creating a focal point, and stepping back regularly to evaluate the balance.
The assistant named Joan Miró, Henri Matisse, Pablo Picasso in his later works, Bridget Riley and Ellsworth Kelly as artists who mastered bold and bright colour palettes.

The user plans to start an abstract piece with a bold and bright palette, using a dominant bright yellow with complementary colours for contrast, and to experiment with layering and texture for depth.
The user is thinking of setting up a small studio in their spare bedroom and asked for suggestions on organising a small art space.

The assistant suggested purging and decluttering first, assessing needs, using the work triangle to place frequently used items, choosing multi-functional furniture, using vertical space, creating a wet zone for messy activities, and adding good lighting.

The assistant also recommended ergonomic seating with a small stool or ottoman, an inspiration board, and storage such as stackable plastic bins, shelves with baskets, pegboards with hooks, rolling art carts and hanging organisers for canvases or paper.

The user plans to purge and declutter the space, then assess their needs and optimise the layout, invest in multi-functional furniture, use vertical space to maximise storage, create a wet zone, and add a comfortable seating area.
The user is hosting a dinner party the weekend of 16-17 April 2022, has been really into baking lately, and asked for a unique dessert idea to serve at the party.

The assistant suggested unique desserts including saffron crème brûlée, matcha tiramisu, raspberry basil sorbet, salted caramel chocolate tart, pistachio rosewater macarons, lemon lavender panna cotta, chocolate chai truffles, orange blossom water pudding topped with toasted almonds, cranberry orange crisp, and espresso granita.

The user loves the matcha tiramisu and salted caramel chocolate tart ideas, has been experimenting with strawberries, and said a strawberry rhubarb crisp they made a few weeks ago, around March 2022, was incredible. The user asked for a savoury dish that would complement the sweet desserts.

The assistant recommended savoury dishes with bright, fresh flavours to cut through the richness of the desserts, such as grilled lemon herb chicken, pan-seared scallops with citrus-ginger beurre blanc, and a roasted vegetable tart with goat cheese.

The assistant also suggested grilled asparagus with lemon-Parmesan vinaigrette, herbed quinoa salad with grilled chicken and citrus, roasted beet salad with walnuts and feta, and grilled shrimp skewers with spicy mango salsa.
The user is making sandwiches with their sourdough bread for the dinner party and asked for fillings that would complement the matcha tiramisu and salted caramel chocolate tart.

The assistant suggested smoked salmon with cream cheese and pickled ginger to pair with the matcha tiramisu, caramelised onion and brie to pair with the chocolate tart, and roasted turkey with fig jam and arugula as sourdough sandwich fillings.

The assistant also suggested grilled chicken with apple and mustard, prosciutto and pear with honey, egg salad with pickled carrots and chives, and grilled ham with pineapple and jalapeño as sandwich fillings.
The user is also making lemon bars for the dinner party. The user recently made a batch with a shortbread crust and a lemon curd made with fresh lemons and eggs, which turned out tangy and sweet.

The assistant advised using high-quality European-style or cultured butter with about 82-86% fat, keeping ingredients cold, not overmixing, using a 1:1:1 ratio of butter, sugar and flour, and removing the shortbread crust once it is lightly golden brown.

The assistant advised chilling the shortbread crust in the pan for at least 30 minutes before baking. For the lemon curd, it advised cooking over a double boiler, tempering the eggs, and cooking until just set and still slightly jiggly in the centre.

The user is excited to make the lemon bars and plans to make croissants from scratch, even though their last croissant attempt did not turn out well, and asked for tips on making flaky, buttery croissants.

The assistant advised using European-style butter with about 82-86% fat and unbleached, unbromated flour, keeping the butter and dough cold, and laminating by folding the dough in thirds and repeating 3-4 times. It also advised rolling to about 1/4 inch (6 mm), cutting with a sharp straight-edged cutter, proofing until doubled in a warm draft-free place, and baking in a steamy oven.
The user is excited to try croissants again and plans to make banana bread with walnuts for the dinner party, having recently made a walnut banana bread batch that turned out amazing.

The user baked a chocolate cake for a friend's birthday party today, 10 April 2022, using a new online recipe that used espresso powder to intensify the chocolate flavour, and the cake turned out amazing.

The assistant suggested using ripe, spotty bananas, mixing wet and dry ingredients separately without overmixing, using buttermilk or a substitute of 1 cup of milk with 1 tablespoon of white vinegar or lemon juice, and not overbaking the bread.

The assistant also suggested combining white and brown sugar, adding walnuts, pecans or chocolate chips, using pure vanilla extract and flaky sea salt or kosher salt, and toasting walnuts at 350°F for 5-7 minutes before chopping.
The user is looking for inspiration for their next baking project and has been really into baking lately.

The assistant suggested flavoured cakes such as lemon-rosemary, orange-almond or chocolate-chipotle, artisanal breads such as sourdough, a whole-grain boule or focaccia, and French pastries such as croissants, pain au chocolat or eclairs.
The assistant also suggested seasonal treats, international bakes such as Japanese mochi, Italian panettone or Mexican conchas, and show-stopping multi-layer cakes or dramatic tarts.

The user has been obsessed with strawberries lately after a baking class at a local culinary school on 20 March 2022. The user was thinking of making a strawberry shortcake and asked for tips on making the perfect shortcake.

The assistant's shortcake tips included using high-protein flour of about 12-13% protein, keeping the butter, cream and egg cold, not overmixing or overbaking, resting the dough for at least 30 minutes, and adding a pinch of salt.

The assistant also suggested turbinado or Demerara sugar for a caramel-like flavour, not oversweetening the strawberries, and letting the shortcakes cool completely before assembling to avoid sogginess.

The assistant's basic strawberry shortcake recipe used 2 cups (250g) high-protein flour, 1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/2 cup (115g) cold unsalted butter, 3/4 cup (180ml) chilled heavy cream and 1 large egg, baked at 375°F (190°C) for 18-20 minutes.

The user plans to use fresh strawberries from the farmer's market, has been buying them by the container and snacking on them, and asked for whipping cream recommendations that are light and fluffy but still hold their shape.

The assistant's whipped cream tips included chilling the bowl and beaters for 10-15 minutes, using heavy cream with 36% fat, whipping only to soft peaks, adding sugar gradually, and using a pinch of salt or a squeeze of lemon juice to stabilise it.

The assistant's whipped cream recipe used 1 cup (240ml) chilled heavy cream, 2 tablespoons granulated sugar, a pinch of salt and optionally 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract, and suggested refrigerating it for up to 2 hours if not used immediately.
The user has been experimenting with sourdough bread and asked whether they could use some of their sourdough starter to make a sourdough shortcake instead of a regular shortcake.

The assistant said a sourdough shortcake could work, but starters are finicky, so the recipe would need adjusting for extra flour or less liquid, a mature and active starter, and a proofing time of 2-3 hours or even overnight.

The assistant's experimental sourdough shortcake recipe used 1 cup (120g) sourdough starter at 100% hydration, 2 cups (250g) bread flour, 1/2 cup (60g) granulated sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 cup (60ml) cold unsalted butter and 1 large egg, baked at 350°F (175°C) for 20-25 minutes.

The user has been experimenting with different flours. They made a batch of cookies with bread flour that turned out chewier than usual, and they use oat flour for pancakes and waffles for a nice nutty flavour. The user asked whether oat flour or bread flour would work better for the sourdough shortcake.

The assistant explained that oat flour adds a nutty flavour and a denser texture but has lower gluten and may need more liquid and longer fermentation. Bread flour adds structure and chewiness but can make the shortcake denser and needs less liquid.

The assistant suggested starting with a small test batch, blending the alternative flour with all-purpose flour to create a hybrid, and adjusting liquid, proofing time and temperature based on how the flour behaves.
The user plans to try bread flour first for the sourdough shortcake, having had good results with it in the past, and wants to see how it affects the texture of the shortcake.
